groups.name: Medicines that prolong the QT interval

src.q: Some azoles, including fluconazole, have been associated with prolongation of the QT interval on the electrocardiogram.

Prolongation of the QT interval, reflecting effects on cardiac repolarisation imparting a risk of developing cardiac arrhythmia and torsades de pointes , have been seen in patients treated with macrolides including clarithromycin
Drugs that are inducers of CYP3A (e.g. rifampicin, phenytoin, carbamazepine, phenobarbital, St. John's wort) may induce the metabolism of clarithromycin.
Domperidone has been associated with prolongation of the QT interval on the electrocardiogram.
The main metabolic pathway of domperidone is through CYP3A4.

notes: BATCH AC (fluconazole, miconazole, aciclovir, oseltamivir, fenticonazole, nystatin). All six have UK product information; none is no-uk-product. BNF/BNFC not accessed (geo-blocked). FORM SUBSTITUTIONS (no UK product for the clinic form; same ingredient and route used, stated in formulations[].note): (1) miconazole 400 mg vaginal suppository - no UK miconazole pessary on emc or MHRA Products; the UK miconazole 20 mg/g vaginal cream SPC (PL 00242/0015) is used and its dosing is marked cream-only. (2) fenticonazole 1000 mg vaginal tablet - no UK 1000 mg product; the UK 600 mg vaginal capsule SPC (PL 04595/0008) is used. (3) nystatin ointment - no UK nystatin-only skin product (only combinations with chlorhexidine, hydrocortisone, clobetasol/neomycin, oxytetracycline/clobetasone, benzalkonium/hydrocortisone); the ointment formulation has no source and no rules; everything else is from the UK oral suspension SmPCs. MICONAZOLE FORMULATIONS: miconazole-oral-gel (route oromucosal, systemic interactions), miconazole-cream, miconazole-vaginal. The engine skips group-based rules of OTHER medicines for local routes, so the oral gel's systemic interactions are written explicitly in miconazole.json with master-list ids. INTEGRATOR: gliclazide.json and glimepiride.json have rules with other='miconazole' and no otherFormulations, so they will also fire for the cream and vaginal forms; consider adding otherFormulations ['miconazole-oral-gel'] (gliclazide's SmPC wording is 'systemic or oromucosal gel'). CONFLICTS BETWEEN UK SOURCES: (a) Miconazole oral gel + warfarin - the prescription-only gel SmPC (emc 14746) says caution with careful monitoring/titration, while the sugar-free 2% gel SmPC (emc 6597) lists warfarin under 4.3 Contraindications; MHRA DSU 2017 says over-the-counter gel must not be used with warfarin and prescribed gel needs close monitoring. Both kept as separate rules (contraindicated + caution). (b) Fluconazole + amitriptyline - fluconazole SmPC says measure levels/adjust dose (monitor), while the amitriptyline SmPC (batch P) lists the combination as not recommended; both kept. (c) Aciclovir pregnancy/breastfeeding - SmPC 'only when benefit outweighs unknown risks' / 'caution', vs BUMPS 'can be used, first choice' and SPS 'can be used, preferred, infant monitoring'. (d) Oseltamivir breastfeeding - SmPC 'may be considered where clear benefit' vs SPS 'preferred choice, infant monitoring'. INFERRED RULES (flagged in concern/action text): miconazole oral gel + atorvastatin set to contraindicated because the gel SmPC contraindicates CYP3A4-metabolised statins 'such as simvastatin and lovastatin' and the atorvastatin SmPC (emc 1059) states atorvastatin is metabolised by CYP3A4; atorvastatin is not named in the miconazole SmPC. New group qt-cyp3a4-substrate (QT-prolonging medicines metabolised by CYP3A4) created to express the fluconazole and miconazole oral gel 4.3 contraindication precisely; members sourced from their own SmPCs: clarithromycin and domperidone only. Diltiazem (its SmPC: 'Diltiazem may lead to QT prolongation' and 'Diltiazem is metabolised by CYP3A4') and ondansetron could qualify but were NOT added (weaker/uncertain QT signal); integrator may decide. A broader fluconazole rule against group:qt-prolonging is set to 'avoid' from SPS ('Do not co-prescribe' triazole antifungals with other QT-prolonging medicines). NEW GROUPS: imidazole-antifungal, antifungal, antiviral, qt-cyp3a4-substrate. Fluconazole added (own SmPC quotes) to azole-antifungal, cyp3a4-inhibitor, cyp2c9-inhibitor, cyp2c19-inhibitor and qt-prolonging, so other medicines' group rules (e.g. escitalopram/domperidone QT rules, CYP3A4-inhibitor rules) now fire with fluconazole. Fenticonazole is NOT in azole-antifungal/imidazole-antifungal: its UK SPC does not name its chemical class (only ATC G01AF12). CONDITIONS USED FROM OTHER BATCHES (not redefined): galactose-intolerance-lactase-deficiency (B), hereditary-fructose-intolerance (E/Z), hereditary-sugar-intolerance (G/Z), swallowing-difficulty (G), respiratory-failure (D), peanut-soya-allergy (D), cardiac-arrhythmia (P). RENAL BOUNDARIES: oseltamivir SmPC bands are '>30 to 60' and '>10 to 30'; the schema has no exclusive minimum, so at exactly 30 or 10 mL/min two bands overlap (stated in the rule action). Oseltamivir renal rules carry age minYears 13 because the SmPC gives no renal dosing for children 12 and under. NOT FOUND: no SPS breastfeeding page for antifungals (fluconazole, miconazole, nystatin, fenticonazole; several URL patterns and SPS search tried); no BUMPS leaflet for miconazole, nystatin, fenticonazole or oseltamivir; no MHRA DSU on fluconazole-specific risks found by keyword search (only statin and clopidogrel articles mention it). Brand-specific prescribing: none stated by any UK source for these six medicines. AUDIT 2026-10-17 (AC), independent second check: (1) miconazole:interaction:atorvastatin-gel changed from contraindicated to info. The contraindication was inferred by combining two SmPCs; no UK source names atorvastatin with miconazole oral gel, so the rule now states only what the sources say (the gel SmPC general CYP3A4 statement and simvastatin/lovastatin named; the atorvastatin SmPC says it is metabolised by CYP3A4). The INFERRED RULES note above is superseded. (2) Fenticonazole added to azole-antifungal and imidazole-antifungal (its SPC 5.3: as for other imidazole derivatives); className updated. This supersedes the note above that its SPC does not name its class. Allergy cross-reactivity rules (miconazole, fluconazole, clotrimazole, miconazole-hydrocortisone) now see fenticonazole; systemic azole interaction rules of other medicines do not fire for it because its route is vaginal. (3) fenticonazole peanut/soya contraindication kept (4.3 of the UK 600 mg capsule) but its concern now says the soya lecithin is an excipient of the UK capsule and the supplied product excipients should be checked. (4) miconazole:condition:swallowing given an extra age limit (under 2 years) and an infant-specific concern: the 4.3 text refers to infants, and the condition swallowing-difficulty is broader (adult dysphagia). (5) fluconazole breastfeeding rule concern qualified (repeated or high doses; single 150 mg dose compatible); statin rules given the discontinue and lower-dose quotes; new info rule fluconazole:interaction:hydrochlorothiazide (+40% fluconazole level, no dose change). (6) aciclovir: new rule aciclovir:age:neonate-cream (avoid; propylene glycol, neonates with open wounds or large areas of broken skin) + cautions item; cream pregnancy quote added to the pregnancy rule. (7) oseltamivir pregnancy item and rule now carry the SmPC qualifier that one study was not conclusive for major congenital heart defects. Reviewed without change: clinic-form substitutions (miconazole 400 mg pessary to UK 20 mg/g vaginal cream; fenticonazole 1000 mg vaginal tablet to UK 600 mg vaginal capsule) are same active, same route, currently on MHRA Products, and the formulation notes say the UK dosing does not apply; nystatin ointment has no UK nystatin-only skin product (emc search shows only combinations), no item or rule is scoped to it; qt-cyp3a4-substrate members (clarithromycin, domperidone) are sourced from their own SmPCs; miconazole warfarin rules (contraindicated per sugar-free gel SmPC 4.3 + MHRA OTC gel; caution per prescription gel SmPC) are scoped to the oral gel and their concerns name the source subgroup.
